correctness.rationale: For any nonempty \(D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\), asking \(f_m^N\) on singleton instance arguments \(\{d_i\}\) with support \(D\) forces every witness neighbourhood \(E\subseteq D\) to contain every \(d_i\), hence \(E=D\). The empty neighbourhood is recovered by \(f_0(; \varnothing)\). Since \(m\le n\), arities through \(n\) reconstruct all neighbourhood memberships. The lower pair \(N^-=\mathcal P(X)\setminus\{X\}\), \(N^+=\mathcal P(X)\) is indistinguishable below \(n\): any successful full-set witness with at most \(n-1\) nonempty instance demands can be replaced by the proper set of one chosen point from each demand; at arity \(n\), the \(n\) singleton demands force \(X\). The bundled checker exhausts all local neighbourhood families through carrier size four and matches this symbolic proof.
residual_risks: Additional frame axioms can reduce the cutoff; the theorem is for arbitrary labelled finite instantial neighbourhood frames.
